item.title: Teen boater found clinging to capsized vessel after 3 go missing; 2 bodies recovered
item.description: The 15-year-old was found suffering from hypothermia after an 18-foot fishing vessel overturned about 4 miles east of St. Lawrence Island.
item.content:encoded:
The United States Coast Guard (USCG) on Tuesday said only one boater, a 15-year-old, was rescued alive after three individuals went missing earlier this week.

Rescue personnel found the teenager "clinging to the capsized vessel" Monday off the coast of Alaska. Officials said crews found him in the midst of a medical emergency.

The "survivor was rescued from the overturned skiff experiencing symptoms of hypothermia," officials said.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

The two other mariners were found dead after the 18-foot fishing vessel they were aboard overturned about 4 miles east of St. Lawrence Island, according to authorities.

The Coast Guard said crews initiated a search mission early Monday after Alaska State Troopers notified the Coast Guard of an overdue boat Sunday evening. The vessel was expected to return Sunday at 3 a.m.

Officials said crews were unable to launch a rescue mission until Monday morning due to weather and poor visibility.

US COAST GUARD SAVES 8, INCLUDING INFANT AND CHILD, AFTER VESSEL CAPSIZES OFF FORT MYERS BEACH

After launching an aircrew, personnel spotted the survivor and deployed a raft with survival equipment.

Officials said a good Samaritan vessel also stepped in, rescuing the 15-year-old survivor and recovering the bodies of the two deceased mariners from the water.

The two mariners and the teen survivor were then brought to Nome, Alaska, officials said.

item.title: Ex-NFL cheerleader battles former gubernatorial aide in tight GOP primary race
item.description: Elaine Pelino and Aaron Guckian are locked in a Rhode Island Republican primary too close to call as the GOP eyes a historically blue state.
item.content:encoded:
Elaine Pelino, a former NFL cheerleader and publisher pitching herself as the party-line choice, and Aaron Guckian, a former aide to former Gov. Donald Carcieri and a more centrist candidate are locked in a GOP primary that remained too close to call by early Thursday morning.

The race centered on experience and qualifications as Republicans hope they have found a candidate to win over a historically Democratic-leaning state.

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES OVERHAUL TO CUT RED TAPE AND SPEED UP AMERICAN ENERGY PROJECTS

In the last election, Daniel McKee, the then-Democratic candidate and current governor of Rhode Island, beat out Republican challenger Ashley Kalus in a 57.9% to 38.9% victory.

Among other priorities in her campaign, Pelino promised to champion merit-based hiring, support law enforcement, immigration law and school choice."This is what I’m going to do. I’m learning. Everything is a learning [curve] because I’m not a lifetime politician. I’m here because I love Rhode Island. And I want them to have a great life. I want them to live in a prosperous and safe place. We should get all the illegals out of here," Pelino said at a candidate forum.

DEM INCUMBENT BECOMES FIRST SITTING GOVERNOR TO LOSE PRIMARY SINCE 2018

Before her time in politics, Pelino had a wide range of experience, working as a model, in media and even as a cheerleader for the Houston Oilers, the football team that would eventually become the NFL’s Tennessee Titans. Later, in 2011, she founded Tigress magazine, which published 12 issues.

For his part, Guckian took a far more policy-centric approach, committing to overhaul Rhode Island’s permitting, improve service delivery and tighten use of the state’s revenue. He argued that the state’s budget growth had "gone too far."

"The state budget increased from $9.3 billion in 2019 to more than $14 billion between 2024 and 2026, nearly 50% growth in five years, even as federal COVID relief dollars are expiring," Guckian said on his campaign website.

"Rhode Island made a critical mistake. We built permanent commitments on temporary federal money."

SELF-FUNDED CEO CLAIMS GOP NOMINATION TO CHALLENGE MASSACHUSETTS DEMOCRAT’S SECOND-TERM BID

Once one of them has secured the primary, Pelino or Guckian will face an uphill battle in the Nov. 3 general election.

item.title: Drake Maye's terrible decision gifts Seahawks opening night win as Patriots left stunned to start NFL season
item.description: Josh Jobe's acrobatic end-zone interception sealed the Seattle Seahawks' 13-10 win, as Drake Maye threw three picks in the NFL season opener.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots went into Lumen Field on Wednesday night and watched as the Seattle Seahawks raised a Super Bowl victory banner commemorating a championship won at their expense.

As a result, Drake Maye, an MVP frontrunner last season who led the Patriots to Super Bowl LX, was hoping for some revenge along with his teammates to start the new year on the right foot.

Instead, it was Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe who got his feet down in the end zone on the final play of Maye’s night, notching Seattle’s third interception of the Patriots quarterback and icing a 13-10 victory in a thrilling finish in the Pacific Northwest.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Maye, the Patriots’ offense, had converted on fourth-and-9 to put themselves in field goal range with less than a minute to play in the NFL’s season opener, and he was hoping this fourth-quarter drive ended with some points, because the other two he had in the quarter ended with interceptions – ones that got Drew Lock and the Seahawks’ offense back in the game.

Yes, it was Lock who played most of the game due to Sam Darnold suffering a hip injury just five snaps into the new season. It was looking bleak for a usually raucous "12’s" fan base in the seats, as a dull murmur fell over Lumen Field when Lock took to the field.

But ultimately, his second-half performance turned the tide, making the most of Maye’s mistakes.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Maye’s biggest came on third-and-5 from Seattle’s 16-yard line, where he scrambled out to his right, and instead of going out of bounds or throwing the ball away, he tried to give Mack Hollins a jump ball in the end zone.

Jobe, though, made an incredible acrobatic catch, contorting his body so both his feet remained in bounds and sealed victory. The "12’s" were in rapture when they saw their stellar defense once again save the day, while the Patriots’ sideline couldn’t believe what just happened.

Maye’s opening night was a roller-coaster. He finished 23-of-33 through the air for 178 yards with one touchdown pass to rookie tight end Eli Raridon – the first of the NFL season – while his three interceptions will be a pain point in team meetings later this week after they watch the tape.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks were thankful for the decision of Maye to not throw it away, as they were at least looking at overtime football with a chip-shot field goal in play before that final interception.

They must also be thankful that Lock was ready to go once Darnold was ruled out the rest of the way. He was highly efficient, as the backup quarterback went 16-of-22 for 187 yards with one touchdown and no turnovers.

And it also helps when the reigning Offensive Player of the Year is locked in to help his backup quarterback find some easy pitch-and-catch scenarios. Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished the night with eight catches for 122 yards, including the game-changing 45-yard catch-and-run touchdown on a clever fourth-and-1 call by the Seahawks to pass instead of run.

Smith-Njigba was wide open and all Lock had to do was hit him in the numbers. From there, the Ohio State product used his blazing speed to get past multiple Patriots defenders and tie the game following the Jason Myers extra point.

That touchdown came after Maye’s first interception, which was hauled in by Nehemiah Pritchett on a deep ball intended for new Patriots receiver Romeo Doubs. No, it wasn’t A.J. Brown, the top offseason acquisition by New England, who was targeted after he suffered an ankle injury that knocked him out of the game like Darnold.

PATRIOTS' AJ BROWN EXITS NFL SEASON OPENER AGAINST SEAHAWKS, RULED OUT WITH ANKLE INJURY

With a tie game, Maye was trying to get the Patriots the lead back, but veteran safety Julian Love had other things in mind. This time, it was a target for Pop Douglas, but Love read Maye the entire way, jumping the route and securing a great field position for Lock and company to work with.

Myers knocked through a 26-yard field goal to end the ensuing drive, and it was the game-winning points for Seattle, who now start the season off 1-0 and make their Super Bowl-winning celebration that much sweeter.

However, all eyes will be on what happens with Darnold later this week, considering their Super Bowl hopes for this season ride on their franchise quarterback being healthy. Darnold landed awkwardly on his knee when Dre’Mont Jones sacked him in the first quarter, and he was noticeably limping to the sideline.

After a trip to the dreaded blue medical tent, Darnold limped his way to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald will learn of his quarterback’s diagnosis soon, and like the rest of the franchise, hope it’s nothing too severe.

The same goes for Brown, whom the Patriots traded for from the Philadelphia Eagles before the start of training camp. He finished his debut with three catches for 26 yards before leaving the game.

item.title: Trump makes stunning first-of-its-kind cash promise in bid to rally GOP voters at Dallas midterm convention
item.description: President Donald Trump promised a $5,000 "Trump dividend" to every adult citizen if Republicans keep Congress at the GOP midterm convention.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — President Donald Trump delivered the keynote speech on day one of the GOP's inaugural midterm convention, alternating between touting his successes in office and rallying thousands of supporters for Republican candidates ahead of November's general election before making a promise to American voters.

In a stunning move, Trump made a promise unheard of in the history of American politics — offering a cash prize should Republicans keep control of Congress.

"I can make this promise to you, and here is my promise," he said. "If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our economic — tremendous economic success like in history, we've never had anything like what's happening. but because of our tremendous strength and success economically — I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000. Very much like a successful company will do a cash distribution to its shareholders."

TRUMP'S UNUSUAL ROLE AT MIDTERM CONVENTION REVEALED AS SCHEDULE GOES PUBLIC

"It will be called the 'Trump dividend,'" he added.

Trump opened the speech by grading his own performance since taking office for a second time in January 2025, saying he's "doing a great job." He quickly shifted to addressing the historical challenge that incumbent parties rarely retain control of Congress in midterm elections.

JOHNSON DOWNPLAYS GOP'S MIDTERM WOES AS DEMOCRATS EYE HOUSE TAKEOVER: 'I AM VERY BULLISH'

"But I say, why is it that no matter how well you're doing, we see not a president — Democrat or Republican — almost never wins the midterms?' said Trump. "We've got to change that because we have something going that's so good we can't let that string be broken. So I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot. I'm on the ballot, just one more time."

During his effort to rally GOP voters to help Republicans hang onto the House and Senate, Trump made sure to give credit to Republicans on Capitol Hill for their work in passing his agenda.

MILLIONS TAP TRUMP TAX CUTS THIS FILING SEASON AS REFUNDS TOP $3,400

"Our Republican Congress puts thousands of dollars into the pockets of working families with the largest tax cuts in the history of our country," he said. "So we had the largest in history. We gave you no tax on tips, no tax on overtime and no tax on Social Security for our great seniors."

He said his administration's efforts on critical issues will be crushed if the GOP loses majorities in either or both chambers of Congress.

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

"Because if we lose, you're going to lose your border," he said. "You're going to lose your tax cuts. You're going to lose your safety and security. You're going to lose your wealth."

Fox News polling shows Trump is underwater with voters on the economy, cost of living and inflation. Sixty-five percent of voters disapprove of his handling of the economy. The president also defended the military conflict in Iran, saying he has received criticism over rising gas prices tied to the conflict but arguing that "I'm right," because Iran was one month away from securing a nuclear weapon. Inflation has risen from 2.4% to 3.4% since the war began in February, while gas prices have also increased.

RECORD GAS PRICES SQUEEZE AMERICANS AS SUMMER TRAVEL SEASON ENDS, MIDTERMS LOOM AND IRAN WAR WAGES ON

Republicans who spoke to Fox News Digital on day one of the convention weren't concerned with Trump's economic policies.

"I believe that Trump is doing the right thing," one RNC attendee told Fox News Digital. "The tariffs are bringing a lot of money back, you know, correcting the national debt. And that's gonna improve everything across the board."

"I feel like as soon as we bring this conflict in Iran to a close, we'll start seeing the full effects of President Trump and the greatness that he's done as far as the economy, the great thing of tariffs, and some of the products of the Trump economy in the golden age," said Jacquez Jones of Texas.

Later, Trump shifted his sights to Texas' high profile U.S. Senate race between Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democrat state Rep. James Talarico.

"We have to elect Ken Paxton," he said, segueing into border security, a top issue under both Trump administrations. "Together, we're going to continue to have — we have the strongest borders now in the history of our country."

'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT

"We have the lowest level of illegal immigration ever recorded in our country," he said, adding that zero illegal immigrants have entered the country through Texas in 16 months.

"And therefore zero have been admitted into Texas where they used to be running around, running rampant, killing people, destroying many houses and farms, and ruining property values and creating havoc all over the state of Texas," he said.

During the speech, he also took aim at Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and former Gov. Roy Cooper in North Carolina.

LONGTIME GOP AIDE DEFECTS TO DEM RISING STAR AS TEXAS SENATE BATTLE FOR CORNYN'S SEAT HEATS UP

He also touted what he described as foreign policy wins. After the arrest of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, Trump boasted about "the biggest oil deal" ever, which he said might be "the biggest deal in the history of our country."

"65 billion barrels are ours," Trump said. "And you know what they say it is lifetime 500 years."

Later, Trump transitioned to slamming the GOP's far-left opponents.

"In this election, the Democrats have nominated the most extreme and dangerous group of candidates for the House and Senate ever to seek office," he said. "These people are radical left communists. Many of them. Not all of them, but many of them in state after state. The Democrat establishment has been overthrown and replaced by crazed lunatics and radicals. They call themselves Democrat socialists. But actually they're communists. They're not socialists. They're long beyond socialists."

He noted the DSA has proposed abolishing prisons, ICE, Border Patrol, the U.S. Senate and the presidency.

That message was one Alex Stone of Kansas City, Missouri, hoped for earlier in the day.

"Tell the truth about who they are, what they believe and what they plan on doing," he told Fox News Digital when asked what Trump's message to Americans should be. "Democratic Socialists of America with El-Sayed in Michigan, in particular, these people want to destroy people like myself. They want to destory people like President Trump and many of the other people here. If they get into power, what is going to happen to us?"

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The president said he's prepared for stiff opposition from those opponents.

"The pundits, the fake news media and the radical left communists will say anything they can to try and stop us. But in this election, all that matters is that we are united, we are together, and what we say counts."

item.title: Patriots' AJ Brown exits NFL season opener against Seahawks, ruled out with ankle injury
item.description: New England Patriots newcomer A.J. Brown walked to the locker room wearing one cleat after receiving medical attention on the field in Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
A.J. Brown’s highly anticipated debut with the New England Patriots was interrupted by an apparent injury in the third quarter of Wednesday’s NFL season opener.

Brown appeared to suffer the injury while trying to make a catch at Lumen Field against the Seattle Seahawks. The game was billed as a rematch of Super Bowl LX, which Seattle won in February by defeating New England 29-10 to claim the franchise’s second Vince Lombardi Trophy.

New England led 10-0 when Brown exited the game Wednesday.

INJURY BUG BITES 49ERS AGAIN AS TEAM LOSES KEY DEFENSIVE TACKLE DURING PRACTICE IN AUSTRALIA

Brown went down after a Seahawks defender rolled into him and remained on the field after the play. After medical personnel tended to Brown on the field, he made his way to the sideline without assistance.

PATRIOTS LOCK UP CHRISTIAN GONZALEZ AS HIGHEST-PAID NFL CORNERBACK JUST BEFORE SEASON OPENER AT SEATTLE

He later entered the blue medical tent before eventually heading to the locker room wearing only one cleat.

Brown was later ruled out for the remainder of the game because of what was described as an ankle injury. He finished his night with three catches for 26 yards. He also drew a 34-yard pass interference penalty that put the Patriots in position for the game's first touchdown.

New England took a 10-3 lead over Seattle into the fourth quarter.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the game in the first quarter and was later ruled out. Drew Lock replaced Darnold under center for Seattle.

item.title: Fetterman teases where his true loyalty lies after surprise appearance at GOP convention
item.description: Senate Democrat John Fetterman drew a hard line after introducing Dave McCormick at the Republican National Committee's midterm convention.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — A rogue Senate Democrat toying with the idea of leaving his party drew a hard line in the sand after making a surprise appearance at the GOP’s Trump-centric convention.

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., has been welcomed with open arms by Republicans to join the party after he floated leaving his own caucus, and spurred further speculation that he would jump ship after dropping a video introducing his colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention on Wednesday.

But in a statement to Fox News Digital, the progressive-turned centrist said that he wasn’t turning his back on the Democratic Party, even as the knives have come out to cut him loose from the Senate.

DEM SENATOR DELIVERS SURPRISE VIDEO AT REPUBLICAN CONVENTION BACKING MCCORMICK

"My remarks introduced Dave McCormick as a great American and friend. We are in different parties, but we are both Team PA," Fetterman said. "We have delivered hundreds of millions of dollars back to Pennsylvania, fought for improved transportation and affordable housing, and the Steel Way of Life."

"I’m a lifelong Democrat who votes overwhelmingly with my party — and should the Senate flip in November, I will still be the 51st vote that I ran on," he continued.

Fetterman started his career in the Senate after besting Dr. Mehmet Oz in a tight race for power in 2022, where he clinched a historically thin Democratic majority in 2022 running on a progressive platform.

TOP REPUBLICAN NAMES WHO HE SAYS IS REALLY LEADING DEMOCRATS — AND IT'S NOT SCHUMER OR JEFFRIES

But since then, he has become a thorn in Democrats’ side, and challenged the direction of the party.

Earlier this year, Fetterman warned that if Democrats became more entrenched in anti-Israel policy positions, he would exit the party, and has taken jabs at the party’s direction during this midterm election cycle as far-left progressives, like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, have emerged as standard-bearers.

Fetterman has routinely bucked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and his colleagues on a handful of key issues, like President Donald Trump’s war in Iran or voting with Republicans to end the marathon government shutdown last Fall.

FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE'

His latest edict followed a bombshell report that alleged through leaked texts with his aides that the maverick Democrat would often brush off duties of his office, like meeting with paralyzed veterans or charging that a three-hour funeral service for slain police officers was a "non-starter."

And Republicans would gladly welcome him into the fold. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said in July that he and others in the Senate GOP have had "had conversations with him in the past … about the challenges he faces in his caucus."

"And, you know, there are many of us who I think would welcome the opportunity to have him join the Republican conference," Thune said.

But for now, Fetterman is staying put even if Democrats flip the Senate in November.

item.title: NBA star Jaylen Brown says in ridiculous interview he's an influencer, not an entertainer for fans
item.description: Jaylen Brown told Mahershala Ali he refuses to be seen as just an entertainer, adding to a long history of quotes that critics call tone-deaf vanity.
item.content:encoded:
If there is one thing Jaylen Brown is truly elite at, besides turning the ball over with his left hand on a crucial drive, it is convincing himself he is the smartest guy in any room he walks into.

The NBA has a long history of foolish quotes, but Jaylen routinely delivers gems so profoundly pseudo-intellectual they belong in a Hall of Fame for tone-deaf vanity.

That is saying something in a league run by LeBron.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Brown, the new Sixers star, recently sat down with Oscar winner Mahershala Ali for a slick Hollywood Reporter feature, and predictable as sunrise, Brown could not stick to basketball.

Instead, we got his latest sermon on why he is far too deep to be categorized as a mere athlete.

"I refuse to adopt the idea that me being an athlete, I’m just here to entertain people," Brown said, apparently rebranding himself from NBA wing to sociopolitical visionary.

"They want our athletes, our musicians, our entertainers, our people of influence to think that we just here for entertainment purposes. I’m going to forever disagree with that."

Right. When millions of fans fork over hard-earned cash for tickets and jerseys, they aren’t looking to kick back on a Tuesday night and watch a game.

They’re obviously tuning in to absorb the profound cultural wisdom of a guy making over $300 million to bounce a leather ball on hardwood.

BOSTON CELTICS STAR JAYLEN BROWN TELLS ESPN'S STEPHEN A SMITH TO 'BE QUIET AND RETIRE'

For years, Brown has cultivated a reputation as the league’s resident philosopher-king, masking questionable judgment behind a wall of academic posturing.

He has never been shy about marveling at his own brainpower. In a 2022 interview with The Ringer, Brown described how people supposedly react when he speaks.

Brown sahred, "When I open my mouth and talk, sometimes people say they are amazed of my intellect. I don’t know if that’s because I truly speak in a way that people can understand or feel a certain way, or because they don’t expect it."

Astonishing stuff.

STEPHEN A SMITH FIRES BACK AT JAYLEN BROWN AFTER CELTICS STAR CALLED HIM THE 'FACE OF CLICKBAIT MEDIA'

When reports surfaced that NBA front-office personnel viewed Brown’s "smartest guy in the room" persona as a locker-room turnoff, Brown addressed the criticism during an Instagram Live session.

"No offense to everybody in sports," Brown declared, "but the bar is f***ing low."

NBA media fanboys love to brag that Brown was an "MIT Fellow."

This is the same guy who claimed he was "undecided" on whether the Earth was flat when Kyrie Irving went down that rabbit hole. He defended Irving’s promotion of an antisemitic film, stuck by Kanye West’s Donda Sports long after everyone else fled and wore a Q-Ray-style magnetic necklace marketed as a device that could supposedly alter the body’s energy frequencies through a smartphone app.

Yet Brown still expects the world to treat him like a generational thought leader who transcends basketball, all while complaining about how unfairly athletes are treated.

In a 2017 interview with The Guardian, Brown complained that athletes were still expected to "shut up and dribble."

Nobody is telling Jaylen Brown to shut up. We’re just asking him to stop acting like he split the atom.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: 25 years after 9/11, ICE says more than 2K known or suspected terrorists have been deported
item.description: ICE arrested over 2,150 known or suspected terrorists and deported more than 2,000 since Trump took office, DHS says ahead of the 9/11 anniversary.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has deported more than 2,000 known or suspected terrorists from the U.S. since President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) tells Fox News Digital, as the nation prepares to mark 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

DHS said ICE arrested more than 2,150 known or suspected terrorists between Jan. 20, 2025, and Sept. 9, 2026, and deported 2,015 during that period.

"As we reflect on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, the brave men and women of ICE continue to carry out their duty to protect the homeland and keep the American people safe," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in the department’s announcement.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

Mullin said ICE had arrested more than 2,100 known or suspected terrorists and deported more than 2,000, adding that the anniversary underscored the department’s commitment to "eternal vigilance."

DHS pointed to several recent cases involving alleged terrorists and members of designated foreign terrorist organizations.

WHITE HOUSE UFC TERROR PLOT 'RINGLEADER' IS A MEXICAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT, DHS CONFIRMS

In June, federal authorities arrested Abraham Hermosillo Alvarez, a Mexican national DHS described as the suspected ringleader of an alleged mass-casualty plot targeting UFC Freedom 250 at the White House.

DHS said Alvarez overstayed a visitor visa that expired in 2001 and later received DACA status in 2014. ICE lodged a detainer following his arrest.

Days earlier, ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) arrested Felipe Linares De Oliveira Dell Aquilla, a Brazilian national DHS identified as a former commander of two designated foreign terrorist organizations.

Authorities said they recovered a handgun, cash and multiple electronic devices after a vehicle and foot pursuit in North Carolina.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SAYS FEDERAL AUTHORITIES HAVE ARRESTED MORE THAN 10,000 SUSPECTED GANG MEMBERS

DHS said Aquilla was wanted in Brazil on criminal association and extortion charges and was allegedly holding his wife against her will while preparing to flee to Mexico.

ICE lodged a detainer after his arrest, while investigators pursued additional firearm and kidnapping charges.

Four Venezuelan members of Tren de Aragua also pleaded guilty in May to charges stemming from a 2024 Bronx shooting that killed two people.

DHS said all four had entered the United States illegally between 2022 and 2023.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: 9/11 IS JUST A HISTORY CHAPTER FOR A NEW GENERATION OF AMERICANS

The announcement comes as the nation prepares to mark 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people in New York City, at the Pentagon and in Pennsylvania.

The attacks prompted the largest overhaul of the nation's homeland security apparatus in decades, including the creation of DHS in 2002 and ICE the following year.

Friday's anniversary will commemorate the victims of the attacks and the first responders who rushed into danger, while marking a quarter-century of U.S. efforts to prevent another large-scale terrorist attack on American soil.

item.title: Researcher who departed AI role over fears of racing into extinction says people are 'begging' for regulation
item.description: Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic researcher who left the company over fears the technology could take over the human race, shared his experience with Fox News.
item.content:encoded:
The Anthropic researcher who is leaving the company over fears the technology is gambling with human life told Fox News there is hope that we can avoid the chance it could destroy humankind within the next decade.

Speaking exclusively Wednesday on "Special Report," Jacob Coxon, 27, said regulation is key.

He posted his resignation Tuesday on X, writing that companies are not acting responsibly and that the race toward self-improving superintelligence is "gambling with our lives."

Coxon, who said he spent the past three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, noted that it's not a completely hopeless scenario.

ANTHROPIC RESEARCHER SAYS AI HAS OVER 10% CHANCE TO 'KILL ALL HUMANS' WITHIN NEXT DECADE

He told Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier the problem is "eminently solvable." 

Evan Hubinger, alignment science lead at Anthropic, expressed his agreement with Coxon's X post.

"Jacob is correct here — we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!" he wrote on X. "I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to."

SANDERS PUSHES 'DEATH PENALTY' FOR CRUCIAL US INDUSTRY THAT COULD GIVE ADVANTAGE TO FOREIGN ADVERSARIES

"To be clear, as we say in our latest Risk Report, I think the risk from present models is low," Hubinger added. "What I am worried about is superintelligence arising from recursive self-improvement, as we have said is happening faster than we thought."

Coxon said he agrees with Hubinger that right now, the threat is "minimal" of artificial intelligence's actual takeover.

"But recursive self-improvement — this AIs making themselves smarter — could happen as soon as next year," he added. "Some people even say six months. So this attitude is shared across the industry, where people essentially are aware that the work they are currently doing, if we don't slow down, could lead to AI takeover by the end of the decade."

He believes there is "definitely" something the country can do to change the dynamic of the "greater than 10% chance" that AI kills all humans.

"I think the problem is not unsolvable, it's not like we think this is some impossible thing — it's just, we're racing so fast, we haven't got time to solve it correctly, we're not being careful, and everyone wants to be careful," Coxon said. "I think it's just — people are begging for regulation. I think it's just a matter of — international — somebody stepping in and being able to ensure that we don't race ourselves into extinction. The problem is eminently solvable."

The technology is being used on the international stage as a "superweapon" in an arms race, Coxon said, calling for the global community to provide oversight.

"This is possibly the most dangerous technology that humanity has ever created," he continued. "It's basically out of science fiction. I think we have no other choice but to cooperate internationally because an arms race would be disastrous in a way that no other human activity has been in the past."

Coxon mentioned that a number of technology leaders have publicly expressed the need for a slow-down agreement, but people are not yet taking them seriously.

"It's not just a marketing stunt," he said. "These people are deadly serious that they think their industry needs to be regulated as soon as possible."

As for AI's benefits, Coxon said we are "on the doorstep of tremendous discoveries," but we're running in too quickly. He emphasized the need for moderation.

Baier asked Coxon if the issue could be figured out.

"I think definitely. I think if we actually try instead of submitting to the inevitability of a doomed race or a hubristic gamble, then we can solve it," he said. "The problem is not unsolvable."

Fox News Digital reached out to Anthropic for comment.

item.title: US Open winner Andy Roddick defends late finishes amid criticism after Ben Shelton-Carlos Alcaraz thriller
item.description: Andy Roddick defended the US Open's late-night scheduling on his "Served" podcast after Ben Shelton's epic win over Carlos Alcaraz ended at 3:33 a.m.
item.content:encoded:
Retired American tennis star Andy Roddick weighed in on Ben Shelton’s five-set victory over Carlos Alcaraz at the U.S. Open, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

Shelton secured the biggest victory of his young professional career in a tiebreaker shortly after 3:30 a.m. ET, becoming the first American man to defeat either Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner at a Grand Slam. His victory, coupled with Frances Tiafoe’s five-set win over fellow American Alex Michelsen in the other men’s quarterfinal, guaranteed that at least one American would reach the 2026 U.S. Open final.

The last time an American-born man brought home the men's singles title at the U.S. Open was in 2003, when Roddick won his lone Grand Slam.

On a recent edition of his "Served" podcast, Roddick addressed criticism surrounding the tournament's late-night schedule and overall logistics, making clear he had no regrets about how the match ultimately turned out.

NOVAK DJOKOVIC SUFFERS STUNNING DEFEAT IN FIRST ROUND OF US OPEN AFTER TRYING TO BATTLE THROUGH AILMENTS

"I know a lot of the comments are, you know, ‘How do you finish at four in the morning?’ and all of that," Roddick said. "Well, every match goes to a match tiebreak except for one. And you’ve got to get 25,000 people out of a stadium responsibly, and you’ve got to get 25,000 people in responsibly. So, I hear a lot of complaining. I don’t hear a lot of proposed solutions."

Roddick stood by the Grand Slam's late-night session format while conceding that a five-hour match could test viewers’ patience, echoing a concern raised by sports podcaster Bill Simmons.

"Starting earlier wasn’t possible because of Frances and Mickelson’s match," Roddick said. "And so, you have to have a night session at the US Open. It’s one of the things that we all love. And they’ve been on the wrong side of luck. Now, I know there are some people who have said shorter format. And I know Bill Simmons made the point that this is ridiculous, that we’re playing too long. He’s normally well-thought-out in his thoughts. I don’t disagree with the premise that, like, ‘Five hours is too much. I’m bored.'"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"7-6 in the fifth last night for Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz in that match, where Tiafoe is down two sets, and the guy’s serving for it — I kind of like the fact that we have a sport where you get into these long-form matches, and it’s the hardest thing on earth," Roddick said. "It’s the hardest sport in the world. If you take that away, can we lay that claim anymore? I don’t know."

Roddick acknowledged the practical case for a shorter format, noting the challenges a late-night match can pose for those working behind the scenes.

"I understand all the pragmatists out there that say we should have a shorter format. I understand the reasons for it. I understand that it’s inconvenient for Sean to be up until 4:00 a.m., you know, watching this match while he’s editing last night’s show," Roddick said. "I understand that some people have to go to sleep because, like you, I had to go to sleep to protect my workday today. I understand all of the rational arguments."

On Friday, Tiafoe and Shelton will meet on center court at Arthur Ashe Stadium, named for the 1968 champion who remains the last Black American man to win the U.S. Open men’s singles title.

item.title: Talarico says he 'missed the mark' as he backtracks on controversial woke statements
item.description: James Talarico now backs banning transgender surgeries for minors and opposing trans athletes in girls' sports as the Texas Senate race heats up.
item.content:encoded:
In a Fox News exclusive interview, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico came out in favor of banning gender surgery for minors and opposed transgender-identifying men competing in women’s sports.

Talarico also backtracked on several of his more controversial claims, including saying there are six genders and that "God is nonbinary."

This comes as the Texas Senate race, which is surprisingly close according to recent Fox News polling, enters its final months. The race is considered critical to both parties' chances of securing a Senate majority. Talarico is facing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican who has faced controversies of his own. A Republican loss in Texas would significantly impact President Donald Trump's ability to implement his agenda.

Fox News spoke with Talarico at a food drive campaign event in Dallas on Tuesday. Talarico’s event took place as the first-ever GOP midterm convention kicked off just miles away in downtown Dallas.

TALARICO CAMPAIGNS WITH SURGEON WHO OPERATED ON TRANSGENDER MINORS: ‘WOLF IN SHEEP’S CLOTHING’

Asked whether he would vote as a U.S. senator in favor of a national ban on gender surgery for minors, Talarico answered, "Absolutely."

He said, "I've been consistent on this issue," explaining his opposition to a Texas bill to ban transgender surgeries on minors by saying the measure "was overly broad."

"If you go back and check, I voted for a major amendment to limit the bill to banning surgeries for minors," he said. "As a lawmaker, my job is to try to sift through everything the bill does. And sometimes there's stuff in it that's really harmful, and I have no choice but to oppose the bill as a whole."

"It's why I try to use amendments, to narrow the focus of the bill so that it does exactly what we intend it to do," he continued. "It's what I tried to do with that piece of legislation, and unfortunately the amendment I supported was unsuccessful."

In 2023, as a member of the Texas House of Representatives, Talarico voted against a state bill titled SB 14, which prohibited certain gender surgery, puberty blockers and certain hormone treatments for minors. There were 18 amendments to the bill proposed by Democrats, all of which Talarico voted in favor and all of which ultimately failed.

In the same interview, Talarico acknowledged that men in women’s sports is a significant issue in Texas. He said, "I oppose trans athletes playing in girls’ sports if it endangers safety or fairness."

"Every sport has to be safe and fair. As a former public school teacher, I care a lot about our student athletes. I care a lot about our students. And so, I will oppose trans athletes playing in girls’ sports if it risks safety or fairness," he said.

Talarico’s comments mark a shift from his earlier position as a Texas state lawmaker. 

In 2021, while serving on the Texas House Public Education Committee, he opposed SB 29, which sought to require public-school athletes to compete based on the biological sex listed on their birth certificate, calling the issue a "manufactured problem." Later that year, he voted against HB 25, which enacted similar restrictions into Texas law.

JAMES TALARICO ADMITS PAST COMMENTS 'MISSED THE MARK' WHEN CONFRONTED ON CLAIMS LIKE GOD IS 'NON-BINARY'

He also addressed perhaps his most controversial statement, which he made in 2021, while opposing a Texas bill to keep men out of women’s sports. Talarico said on the state House floor that "God is both masculine and feminine and everything in between. God is non-binary."

"I was being provocative with that statement. I get that," Talarico admitted, explaining, "What I was trying to say is that you can't use human categories to define God, and that's not controversial theologically. In fact, the late Charlie Kirk, the late Pope Benedict all said the same thing."

Talarico continued, claiming "these comments are being clipped out of context to try to distract from Ken Paxton's career of corruption."

"You mentioned [Paxton] being acquitted in the state Senate. That was after two of his billionaire megadonors gave the lieutenant governor a $3 million check to buy his acquittal," Talarico said. "So, Ken Paxton is the most corrupt politician in Texas and he's gonna try to clip some of my comments, including comments where I was being a little provocative in order to try to distract from that career."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Paxton campaign for a response.

LONGTIME GOP AIDE DEFECTS TO DEM RISING STAR AS TEXAS SENATE BATTLE FOR CORNYN'S SEAT HEATS UP

Regarding his past comment about there being more than two genders, Talarico said he does not currently believe there are six sexes.

"I've missed the mark on some of my past statements. I will be the first to admit it," he said. "What I meant is that there are two sexes, and then there's a small percentage of people with genetic abnormalities."

"Obviously didn't say it correctly. There are not six sexes. There are two, and I think the reason that politicians in that convention center across the street want to talk about six sexes is because they don't want to talk about $6 diesel," he said.

Though he walked back these controversies, Talarico did not hold back on his criticism of the Supreme Court, which he described as "infected" with corruption, saying it "needs to be overhauled."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

He said that if elected, "You're going to expect that I will vote for overhaul to the Supreme Court. That will include binding codes of conduct for our justices. It'll include term limits, and I am open to a discussion about expanding the number of justices."

Following these controversies, Talarico pledged to keep his message focused on affordability for the remainder of the campaign.

"Everywhere I go across the state of Texas, people are struggling to survive in this economy. They are struggling to afford the basics: groceries, gas, utilities, healthcare. And that's what I'm going to be focused on from now until Election Day."

On the topic of affordability, Talarico said that "we should not have a state income tax" in Texas. This is despite Talarico previously voting against a measure to permanently ban a state income tax, which he suggested was redundant and an example of "government waste at its worst." 

The measure was ultimately passed by the Texas Legislature and approved by Texas voters in November 2019.

item.title: George W Bush recalls moment with Derek Jeter before nerve-wracking pitch at Yankee Stadium after 9/11
item.description: Former President George W. Bush recalls throwing the ceremonial first pitch at Yankee Stadium weeks after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
item.content:encoded:
Former President George W. Bush recalled Wednesday a lighthearted moment he shared with New York Yankees shortstop Derek Jeter before throwing out a ceremonial first pitch at Yankee Stadium just weeks after 9/11.

Bush told the story alongside Condoleezza Rice, his national security advisor at the time of the attacks, during a reunification event at the George W. Bush Presidential Center in Dallas, Texas. 

During the World Series in October 2001, Bush said he was feeling the pressure of leading the nation through a fragile moment when Jeter told him before the game, "Don’t bounce it, they’ll boo you." 

As the audience chuckled at the joke, Bush recalled feeling the raw emotions inside the NYC stadium as he walked to the mound at center field.

GEORGE BUSH WELCOMES TOP OFFICIALS TO HIS HOME STATE FOR 9/11 REMEMBRANCE ON 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF ATTACKS

"I looked at the catcher, he looked really tiny, and the ball felt really heavy," Bush said.

While scanning the faces in the crowd, Bush said he could imagine people thinking, "You can knock down our buildings, but you d— sure not going to touch our soul."

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

Bush recalled throwing the ball, which made it over the plate, and described the moment as "memorable."

"I mean, it was an amazing feeling," he said.

This coming Friday will mark the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, when al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four commercial airplanes in a coordinated attack against the United States. 

Two of the flights struck New York City’s Twin Towers at the World Trade Center, sending both buildings crashing down and causing mass casualties. A third flight struck the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., while the fourth crashed in a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

Nearly 3,000 people died in the terror attacks, including hundreds of firefighters and police officers.

item.title: US forces obliterate suspected 'narco-terrorist' vessel in lethal Eastern Pacific strike, killing 3
item.description: A U.S. military strike destroyed a suspected drug-smuggling vessel in the Eastern Pacific, killing three alleged narco-terrorists, officials said.
item.content:encoded:
A suspected drug-smuggling vessel was wiped out in a lethal U.S. military strike Wednesday in the Eastern Pacific, killing three alleged "narco-terrorists" aboard, according to the Department of War.

Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere carried out the Sept. 9 strike under the direction of U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) after intelligence allegedly tied the vessel to drug trafficking.

"Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking," the department said in a post on X. "The operation killed three narco-terrorists."

WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES

The operation marked the latest U.S. attack on suspected cartel vessels accused of moving deadly narcotics along known trafficking routes off the coast of Latin America.

It came less than two weeks after the Pentagon released newly unclassified images to Fox News Digital showing suspected drug boats speeding across open water, including one vessel loaded with what appeared to be bundles of narcotics.

The images, dated Oct. 27, Oct. 29 and Dec. 4, 2025, offered a rare look at suspected smugglers under U.S. military surveillance as the Trump administration intensified its campaign against cartel networks.

EXCLUSIVE: FENTANYL DEATHS PLUNGE 22% AS TRUMP WHITE HOUSE TOUTS CRACKDOWN ON DEADLY DRUG CRISIS

Pentagon press secretary Kingsley Wilson accompanied the release with a deadly warning for traffickers who threaten American communities.

"Nearly one year after the first strike, the message to narco-terrorists remains unchanged: if you traffic deadly illicit narcotics and threaten the American people, we will hunt you down, we will find you, and we will kill you," Wilson told Fox News Digital at the time.

The Pentagon said Operation Southern Spear had carried out 67 strikes as of late August, beginning with the first operation on Sept. 2, 2025.

US MILITARY BOARDS, SEARCHES AND SINKS VESSEL ALLEGEDLY SUPPORTING LOS CHONEROS NARCO-TERRORISTS

Wilson said the campaign had disrupted trafficking networks, forced smugglers to change their tactics and removed "dangerous narcoterrorists."

"Operation Southern Spear has disrupted trafficking networks, forced trafficker adaptations, removed dangerous narcoterrorists, and demonstrated that the United States will use every lawful tool available to defend our Homeland and protect our communities," Wilson said.

One of the most recent strikes came Aug. 25, when U.S. Southern Command said four alleged drug smugglers were killed aboard a fast boat operating along known trafficking routes in the Caribbean.

"Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking," SOUTHCOM said at the time.

US FORCES SINK NARCO-REFUELING STATION LINKED TO ECUADORIAN CARTEL IN PACIFIC: SOUTHCOM

The operation was carried out by Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere under the direction of Gen. Francis L. Donovan.

"Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere continues executing precise, lethal operations against the cartels," Donovan said. "We will hunt, disrupt, and defeat these narco-terrorist networks."

"SOUTHCOM is resolved to neutralizing cartel terror and violence throughout the region and into the U.S. homeland," he added.

Days before that Caribbean strike, the U.S. military said two people were killed in an attack on a vessel in the Eastern Pacific. It was the first reported strike in more than two months.

US MILITARY KILLS THREE 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN LATEST LETHAL STRIKE ON VESSEL IN THE EASTERN PACIFIC

President Donald Trump has described the fight as an "armed conflict" with cartels in Latin America and argued the attacks are necessary to stop drugs from reaching American communities and fueling fatal overdoses.

The administration is also pursuing agreements with allied nations that could extend the campaign onto land in several Latin American countries.

War Secretary Pete Hegseth said during an August visit to Panama that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the U.S. to conduct joint operations against criminal groups on their soil, though Guatemala denied that an agreement had been reached. Ecuador began similar missions with the U.S. in March.

Fox News Digital's Eric Mack contributed to this report.

item.title: Bryce Underwood addresses Kyle Whittingham's comments about remaining starting QB at Michigan
item.description: Michigan Wolverines QB Bryce Underwood feigned ignorance when asked about Kyle Whittingham questioning his starting job after the Week 1 win.
item.content:encoded:
The Michigan Wolverines became the story of Week 1 of the college football season as a result of their underwhelming performance in the "win" over Western Michigan.

After time seemingly expired, officials added an additional second to the clock after replay review. Which Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood used to his advantage. While his first attempt sailed out of the back of the end zone, the second try fell perfectly to wide receiver JJ Buchanan for the walk-off winner.

It was Underwood's best play of the game, not too surprising considering it was a game-winning Hail Mary. But what was surprising was just how bad he looked for the previous 60 minutes. Really, really bad. For someone whose recruitment turned into a bidding war, with well-heeled donors pushing him to Ann Arbor.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN

Excluding the Hail Mary, Underwood completed just 11 passes on 21 attempts for 127 yards. He had much more success in the running game, with nine rushes for 47 yards and a touchdown. But he frequently looked indecisive as a passer, overthrowing or underthrowing receivers and frequently looking confused in a new offense.

After the game and his performance, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham wasn't exactly effusive with praise. Whittingham said Underwood was the starter "right now," but heavily implied that his role would be reevaluated, perhaps sooner rather than later.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"He's our QB right now. It's not something that's infinite," Whittingham told reporters on Monday. "At some point, we've got to turn a corner, and we've got to see improvement.

"As we do with a bunch of stuff, we've got to see improvement out of the coaches. It's not just Bryce; it's not just Bryce's job that is not absolutely set in concrete. Nobody's is, you've got to perform week in and week out. Become somebody that we feel is playing at a level that we can win with."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

For a quarterback who got $12 million in NIL to start at Michigan, that's underwhelming at best and potentially career changing at worst. On Wednesday, Underwood spoke to the media and was asked about Whittingham's comments. And instead of responding head on, he feigned ignorance.

"Um, there was comments about that?" he said. After he was reminded of Whittingham's remarks, he answered "That's cool. I didn't see that. It's cool."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The full video of the interaction was even more painful to see than the answers indicated.

Your head coach says your job might be up for grabs if things don't improve quickly, and you expect people to believe that you didn't hear about it until days later, when asked by reporters? That's obviously not what happened, but it is telling that Underwood choose to respond like this.

Whatever answer he gave could have been obviously pre-rehearsed, but it would instill more confidence to acknowledge the poor play this past weekend, and express confidence that better play is ahead. Particularly when the Wolverines have no time to rest, with an even tougher matchup against the Oklahoma Sooners looming this coming weekend.

Underwood still has the immense arm strength, potential, and passing ability that he had coming out of high school, but to this point in his career, it's been mainly visible in short bursts and not through him consistently dominating games. He's still young, and still just one game into his sophomore season, but if Underwood doesn't improve in a hurry, college football fans might quickly turn to labeling him one of the biggest busts of the NIL era.

item.title: Dem senator delivers surprise video at Republican convention backing McCormick
item.description: John Fetterman's surprise video at the GOP convention praised Trump and Dave McCormick while rejecting what he called Democratic "extremes and socialism."
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., delivered a surprise video message at the GOP midterm convention Wednesday night, praising President Donald Trump and Republican Sen. Dave McCormick while rejecting what he described as the Democratic Party’s "extremes and socialism."

"I’m a commonsense Democrat. I’m always going to stand with America," Fetterman said. "I’m always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life."

Fetterman introduced McCormick, who is seeking re-election to the Senate, as "the kind of senator that gets the job done" and someone who will "fight for Pennsylvania."

FETTERMAN LEANS ON UNLIKELY GOP ALLY AS DEMS SHARPEN THEIR KNIVES OVER EXPLOSIVE REPORT

Standing in front of an iconic U.S. steel mill, Fetterman said he was proud to work with McCormick and Trump to defend Pennsylvania’s steel industry, which remains a central part of the state’s economic and political identity.

"That’s exactly the kind of thing that we will work together and will work with President Trump to fight and defend the steel way of life right here in the Steel Valley," Fetterman said.

The message was notable because Fetterman is a sitting Democratic senator appearing at the Republican Party’s first midterm convention, where Trump is expected to rally GOP voters ahead of the Nov. 3 elections.

His appearance also highlighted his increasingly strained relationship with Democratic leaders and the party’s left wing. Fetterman has repeatedly broken with Democrats on issues including Israel, immigration and Trump’s military actions against Iran.

He has remained one of the most outspoken Democratic supporters of Israel in the Senate and has criticized members of his party who have sought to limit U.S. support for the country. Fetterman has also backed tougher immigration enforcement and supported some Trump administration nominees, positions that have drawn criticism from Democrats.

Fetterman has said he would consider leaving the Democratic Party if it became "the anti-Israel party," though he has not indicated that he plans to switch parties.

The senator’s relationship with McCormick has also fueled speculation about his political future. The two Pennsylvania senators previously faced one another in the 2022 Senate race, when Fetterman defeated Republican nominee Mehmet Oz and McCormick lost the GOP primary.

CAN THE 'BEST SHOWMAN IN POLITICS' DELIVER AGAIN? GOP BETS ON TRUMP AT HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION

Since then, Fetterman and McCormick have developed an unusually close relationship. Their campaigns formed a bipartisan joint fundraising committee in July, an arrangement that drew attention because the two senators belong to opposing parties.

McCormick has also sought to emphasize his ties to Pennsylvania’s industrial base and his support for the state’s steelworkers. Fetterman’s video allowed him to reinforce that message while presenting McCormick as a senator willing to work across party lines.

The appearance does not mean Fetterman is switching parties, but it is likely to intensify questions about whether he can maintain support from Democratic voters as he continues to align himself with Trump and Republican priorities.

It also gives Republicans a high-profile Democratic voice to showcase as they argue that the party’s coalition is expanding beyond traditional GOP voters.

"A different party," Fetterman said of McCormick. "But I’m proud to count him as my great friend."

item.title: Democratic student group to protest Charlie Kirk memorial at campus where he was killed
item.description: Turning Point USA planned a Charlie Kirk memorial at Utah Valley University, but UVU's Students for a Democratic Society have organized a protest against the event.
item.content:encoded:
Turning Point USA (TPUSA) will be hosting a memorial for its founder Charlie Kirk, who was killed at Utah Valley University (UVU), on the first anniversary of his death, and a student group is planning a protest.

In a press release, TPUSA announced, "Turning Point USA will hold the ‘Freedom Built to Last Memorial’ on Sept. 10 to honor the faith-filled husband, father, and defender of free speech with a memorial that serves as a deliberate act of remembrance and a call for students and supporters to continue his life’s work."

The livestreamed event, which begins at 6:30 p.m. MT, will feature speeches by radio host Glenn Beck, Christian author Frank Turek and TPUSA officials.

Utah Valley University announced last month it would cancel classes and close its campus Sept. 10 for a day of healing, service and connection.

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

However, some students have voiced opposition to the event.

According to The Salt Lake Tribune, UVU’s Students for a Democratic Society club opposes the memorial and is planning to protest it Thursday evening before the TPUSA event begins. The group penned an open letter to campus administration that has reportedly been signed by more than 600 people.

"We, students of UVU, strongly condemn the decision to hand over our campus to TPUSA on September 10. As we approach the anniversary of this tragic event, it should be made clear that many of us will be further negatively affected by allowing TPUSA to occupy our campus on that day," students said in the open letter addressed to the campus administration.

"By closing the campus for the entire day ‘to provide time and space’ and emailing all students with details about the far-right political event hosted at our UCCU Center, President Anderson has aligned himself with the interests of Charlie Kirk’s openly racist and antagonistic organization, which intends to use a narrative of victimhood to provide cover for its campaign to advance chauvinistic and divisive ideas within our university."

GEORGETOWN STUDENTS PLAN CHARLIE KIRK 'LOOKALIKE CONTEST' ON ANNIVERSARY OF HIS ASSASSINATION

According to the Tribune, UVU President Jon Anderson stressed the event is not sponsored by the university, but the school would be providing security. He defended allowing TPUSA to host the event on campus.

"As an institution, it’s important that we stay apolitical, that we don’t jump in the fray," he said. "Any entity could’ve used that space, and they chose to have that day. And we allowed them to do that."

Fox News Digital reached out to UVU and TPUSA for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold suffers hip injury, ruled out just five snaps into NFL season
item.description: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is ruled out of the team’s season opener against the New England Patriots after just five snaps.
item.content:encoded:
Just five snaps into the new NFL season, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was back in the locker room with an injury. 

Darnold was sacked during the Seahawks' first series of the season by New England Patriots linebacker Dre'Mont Jones, and he appeared to land awkwardly on his side. 

When the Seahawks went back to the sideline to punt away, Darnold was noticeably limping. He eventually went into the blue medical tent, and after deliberation from the Seahawks' medical team, he began limping his way to the locker room. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Darnold is now officially questionable to return, as Drew Lock took over at quarterback for Seattle. 

There was nothing malicious about Jones’ play as he tracked down Darnold. The issue came from his fall onto the Lumen Field turf.

Darnold seemed fine initially when he began jogging to the sideline, but the limp slowly came in. NBC/Peacock play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico noticed Darnold's gait, calling it out over the NFL's first broadcast of the year. Surely enough, he went into the medical tent and hasn't returned since. 

It goes without saying how important Darnold is to the Seahawks franchise. He's a big reason why the team was able to lift another Super Bowl banner on Wednesday night, as the loyal "12s" cheered for the victory that came at the expense of these same Patriots back in February.
