Darnold, who was coming off a 14-3 season with the Minnesota Vikings that revitalized his career as a starter, matched that same regular-season record in his first year with Seattle in 2025. He threw for 4,048 yards with 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions, completing 67.7% of his passes. 

In the postseason, Darnold threw five touchdowns across the Seahawks’ three victories with no interceptions. 

Now, the Seahawks and its fan base will hope that whatever injury he is dealing with won't be serious enough to miss significant time. 

Meanwhile, Lock backed up Darnold in 2025 after spending a previous season in Seattle in 2023. He served as the backup for the New York Giants as well before getting five starts in 2024. 

Over Lock’s career, he’s earned 28 starts, going 10-18 over that span. He has thrown for 6,369 yards with 34 touchdowns and 28 interceptions over 41 appearances.

item.title: Drone nearly strikes Zelenskyy’s plane before takeoff for Norwegian king’s funeral, PM says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was reportedly almost hit by a Russian drone during takeoff from Moldova, closing Chișinău airspace.
item.content:encoded:
A plane carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to Norway for the king’s state funeral was "almost hit" by a drone as it prepared to take off from Moldova on Tuesday, according to Reuters.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre told public broadcaster NRK about the incident Wednesday, the outlet said, after Zelenskyy’s aircraft arrived safely in Oslo Tuesday evening.

"His plane was almost hit by a drone as it was about to take off from Moldova. That is the reality he is facing," Støre said, without specifying how close the drone came to the Ukrainian leader's aircraft.

GERMANY BLAMES RUSSIA AFTER EXPLOSIVE-LADEN DRONE FOUND NEAR UKRAINIAN CARGO PLANES AT MAJOR AIRPORT

Later Wednesday, a Moldovan government spokesperson said two Russian drones were involved in the incident, with Zelenskyy’s departure to Oslo delayed after authorities closed the country’s airspace.

His aircraft was then cleared for takeoff once officials determined that one Russian drone had landed on Moldovan territory, a spokesperson told Reuters.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

One landed in a field north of the capital, sparking a fire, while the other continued into Romanian airspace.

The incursions forced Chișinău International Airport to temporarily suspend arrivals and departures Tuesday, sending incoming flights into holding patterns or diverting them to neighboring countries, according to tracking data.

RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

Moldovan President Maia Sandu denounced the incursions as a "serious threat to people’s lives" and separately condemned a Russian drone strike on a border crossing with Ukraine that killed two people.

Zelenskyy arrived in Oslo Tuesday evening, where he discussed military aid, including air defense support and civilian assistance with Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide and Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg, according to Deutsche Welle.

The Institute for the Study of War also said a Russian Shahed drone flew through Moldovan and Romanian airspace for about an hour Tuesday before crashing in Moldova.

item.title: HSI agent who investigated child exploitation cases indicted on rape and child abuse charges
item.description: A Homeland Security Investigations agent who worked child exploitation cases faces rape, incest and sodomy charges involving a juvenile in Alabama.
item.content:encoded:
A Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) special agent who investigated child exploitation cases has been indicted on rape, incest and multiple child sex abuse charges involving a juvenile girl in Alabama, authorities said.

A Baldwin County grand jury indicted Kent Blacklidge, 43, on charges of first-degree rape, second-degree rape, first-degree sodomy, second-degree sodomy, two counts of first-degree sexual abuse, two counts of second-degree sexual abuse and incest, according to the Spanish Fort Police Department.

Police said investigators opened the case Jan. 11 after receiving a report alleging the sexual abuse of a juvenile female. 

Blacklidge was placed on administrative leave shortly after the investigation began, authorities said.

OHIO POLICE CHIEF ARRESTED IN FLORIDA AFTER GRAND JURY HANDS DOWN 70-COUNT CHILD SEX INDICTMENT

"It takes an unbelievable amount of courage and strength for a victim of these types of crimes to come forward," Spanish Fort Police Chief John Barber said. "And I commend our victim for having that resolve."

Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall said his office is prosecuting the case after the Baldwin County District Attorney's Office recused itself because Blacklidge is a witness in other cases it handles.

Marshall said the allegations are especially troubling because Blacklidge's duties with HSI included investigating child exploitation cases and helping educate the public about crimes against children.

TRUMP SIGNS HAWLEY MEASURE ADDING 200 CHILD EXPLOITATION INVESTIGATORS IN LARGEST CRACKDOWN EFFORT YET

"He was directly involved in child exploitation cases," Marshall said. "It's why it is so profoundly disappointing and frankly disgusting to stand here today and tell you that we've charged him with facts consistent with what his professional responsibility was."

Authorities said there is one known juvenile victim and no indication of additional victims. Barber declined to discuss further details because of the ongoing case.

Blacklidge turned himself in Sept. 5 after investigators contacted his attorney, officials said. Marshall said if Blacklidge posts bond, he will be subject to electronic monitoring and home confinement and prohibited from contacting the alleged victim or anyone younger than 18.

A Homeland Security Investigations spokesperson declined to comment, citing the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Dem incumbent becomes first sitting governor to lose primary since 2018
item.description: Costco board member, former CVS exec avenges narrow 2022 loss to Gov. Dan McKee in high-stakes Rhode Island rematch. McKee is the first sitting governor to lose aparty primary in years.
item.content:encoded:
Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee lost his Democratic primary Wednesday to businesswoman Helena Foulkes, becoming the first sitting governor in the country since 2018 to be denied his party's nomination.

Foulkes, a former CVS executive and current Costco board member, defeated McKee in a rematch of their closely fought 2022 Democratic primary, when McKee edged her by just a few percentage points. 

McKee's defeat Wednesday adds another incumbent to a growing list of officeholders ousted during the 2026 primary season.

McKee first became governor in 2021 after Gov. Gina Raimondo left office to serve as Commerce Secretary in the Biden administration. The former Cumberland mayor and two-term lieutenant governor went on to win his first full term in 2022 after narrowly emerging from a crowded Democratic primary that included Foulkes.

INCUMBENT GOP GOVERNOR ROLLS TO PRIMARY VICTORY AFTER KEEPING TRUMP AT A DISTANCE

The last sitting governor to lose his party's nomination was Kansas Republican Gov. Jeff Colyer. Colyer lost the 2018 GOP primary to then-Kansas Secretary of State Kris Kobach, backed by Donald Trump at the time, by fewer than 400 votes.

Foulkes has spent decades in the private sector, including as a senior executive at Rhode Island-based CVS Health, and later served as CEO of Hudson's Bay Company. She sits on Costco's board of directors.

Her 2026 campaign marked Foulkes' second bid for elected office after finishing second to McKee in the 2022 Democratic gubernatorial primary.

EX-DEM LOBBYIST FOR COMPANY THAT PROMOTED ADDICTIVE OPIOID CLEARS KEY GUBERNATORIAL HURDLE

The rematch centered in part on the candidates' competing arguments over their records and leadership.

Foulkes criticized McKee's management of state government, including his administration's handling of the Washington Bridge, which was abruptly closed over structural concerns in December 2023 and remains under reconstruction.

McKee defended his administration's record and repeatedly targeted Foulkes' tenure at CVS, suggesting she is an out-of-touch corporate executive and going after her leadership role at the company amid its controversial handling of prescription opioids.

Foulkes will advance to the November general election as a favorite against the winner of the Republican primary between Aaron Guckian, the GOP's 2022 nominee for Rhode Island lieutenant governor, and retired business executive Elaine Pelino. 

Independent candidates Ken Block, Jasjit "Jay" Gotra and Christopher "CD" Reynolds will also be part of the general election action in November, according to The Rhode Island Current.

item.title: Illegal alien ordered removed years ago charged in crash that killed newly engaged 23-year-old teacher
item.description: Cameron Lyon, a newly engaged Ohio teacher, was killed when a previously deported illegal immigrant allegedly flipped his SUV into oncoming traffic.
item.content:encoded:
A previously deported illegal alien allegedly drove drunk before flipping his SUV into oncoming traffic and killing a newly engaged Ohio teacher, authorities said.

Alvaro Uribe-Gonzalez, a 33-year-old Mexican national who federal officials say illegally returned to the U.S. after being deported, now faces aggravated vehicular homicide and other charges in the death of 23-year-old Cameron Lyon.

Lyon’s fiancée, 23-year-old Abrielle Kerns, was seriously injured in the fiery Sunday evening crash on U.S. Route 33 in Fairfield County, according to her family.

The Ohio State Highway Patrol initially described Kerns’ injuries as non-life-threatening, but relatives said she remained in intensive care "fighting to recover" as the family grappled with Lyon’s death.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND

"This is an unconscionable tragedy because it was preventable," Republican Ohio gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy wrote. "This perpetrator shouldn’t have ever been in our country, let alone permitted to remain here."

Ramaswamy pointed to Uribe-Gonzalez’s alleged drunken driving and immigration history as he vowed to take action if elected governor.

"But he ended up driving drunk & killed an innocent young man in Ohio. I won’t tolerate this in our state," Ramaswamy wrote. "So devastating. It doesn’t have to be this way. I’ll fix it in Ohio next year & will go hard as necessary."

The Ohio State Highway Patrol said Lyon was driving west when Uribe-Gonzalez’s eastbound GMC Terrain went off the right side of the highway shortly after 6 p.m.

DAD OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT DUI VICTIM ISSUES WARNING TO AMERICANS OVER LAX DRIVER'S LICENSE LAWS

Uribe-Gonzalez allegedly overcorrected, veered across the roadway and overturned into the westbound lanes, slamming into Lyon’s Chevrolet Trax. The GMC then caught fire.

Lyon was treated at the crash site but died a short time later, the patrol said. Uribe-Gonzalez suffered minor injuries.

Investigators said alcohol is suspected to have played a role in the crash.

Uribe-Gonzalez was charged with aggravated vehicular homicide, driving under the influence of alcohol and operating a motor vehicle without a valid license.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer with the Fairfield County Jail the day after his arrest, asking local officials not to release him before federal agents can take custody.

ILLEGAL ALIEN CHARGED WITH KILLING 4 YOUNG PEOPLE IN WRONG-WAY DUI CRASH ON OKLAHOMA HIGHWAY

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said Uribe-Gonzalez first entered the country illegally through Texas in January 2020 and was arrested by Border Patrol.

An immigration judge issued a final removal order Jan. 11, 2020, and the Trump administration deported him to Mexico April 14 of that year, according to DHS.

Federal officials said Uribe-Gonzalez later illegally crossed back into the U.S. at an unknown date and location.

"This illegal alien has been charged with aggravated vehicular homicide and driving under the influence of alcohol after allegedly causing a car crash that killed 23-year-old Cameron Lyon in Ohio," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

ICE URGES NORTH CAROLINA TO KEEP ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN TRIPLE-FATAL HIT-AND-RUN BEHIND BARS

"Cameron had his whole life ahead of him, and that life was stolen by this criminal who never should have been in our country in the first place."

Mullin said ICE wants Ohio officials to cooperate with the detainer so Uribe-Gonzalez can be taken into federal custody and removed from the country.

Lyon had recently begun his first teaching job and was well-loved by staff and students at Crestline Exempted Schools, according to a fundraiser for his family.

A graduate of Otterbein University, Lyon was remembered as a cherished son, brother and friend whose death left his family and community devastated.

THREE-TIME DEPORTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH KILLING NORTH CAROLINA GIRL, 6, AFTER RUNNING STOP SIGN

Lyon and Kerns had recently become engaged and were preparing to begin their life together. The couple had moved into a home that had been in Lyon’s family for generations and were renovating it together, according to Earthly Pottery Co., where Kerns worked.

"We are devastated by this needless tragedy and miss him dearly," organizers of the fundraiser for Lyon’s family wrote.

A separate fundraiser organized by Kerns’ aunt and uncle said the family was standing beside her through the "shock, pain and uncertainty" of the difficult days following the crash.

"Everyone who knew Abrielle and Cameron could see the love they shared and the future they were building together," the family wrote.

ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF KILLING DAD, TRYING TO FLEE AFTER DRUNKEN CRASH – FEDS RIP BIDEN-ERA RELEASE

The money raised will help cover Kerns’ medical bills and the mounting challenges she faces as she recovers and begins rebuilding her life without Lyon.

"Her world has been turned upside down, and the physical and emotional hardships ahead will be enormous," organizers wrote.

The tragedy has rippled through the community as local businesses rallied around Kerns and Lyon’s family.

Millersport Coffee announced it will donate a portion of its weekend sales to support Lyon’s family and help cover Kerns’ medical needs.

"The entire Kerns family is like family to us," the coffee shop wrote. "We are incredibly thankful that she survived, while we grieve with her and the Lyon family over the heartbreaking loss of her fiancé, Cameron Lyon."

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO KILLED NASHVILLE RESTAURANT OWNER TO FACE ICE DEPORTATION AFTER PRISON

Earthly Pottery Co. said Kerns had helped teach its classes, while Lyon was always willing to lend a hand when the business needed help.

"Their little lives were taking shape and we got a front row seat," the business wrote. "We were texting earlier in the day about getting her studio all set up."

The shop summed up the loss now gripping those who knew Lyon.

"A family has lost a son, a brother, a classroom has lost their teacher, friends have lost their friend," Earthly Pottery Co. wrote.

The crash remains under investigation.

item.title: Veteran Dem senator cruises past far-left primary challengers in bid for sixth term
item.description: Sen. Jack Reed, D-R.I., defeated two far-left challengers in the Rhode Island U.S. Senate primary Wednesday, advancing to the November general election in his bid for a sixth term.
item.content:encoded:
Rhode Island Democratic Sen. Jack Reed fended off two progressive primary challengers Wednesday, extending a three-decade hold on his party's nomination as the 76-year-old senator seeks a sixth term in Washington.

Reed defeated Connor Burbridge, a "small business owner, elder-care worker, community organizer and a working-class Rhode Islander," according to his campaign website, and Luis Muñoz, a medical school graduate, med tech entrepreneur and former candidate who previously ran for Rhode Island governor in 2018 and 2022, according to Muñoz's LinkedIn profile and local reporting about his previous runs.

The victory sends Reed to the November general election against Republican Ray McKay, who ran unopposed in his primary, and independent Michael Bahry.

DEM ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS LONGTIME INCUMBENT FENDS OFF PROGRESSIVE CHALLENGER

Reed's father was a World War II veteran and janitor from Cranston, Rhode Island, before eventually working his way up to becoming a custodial supervisor of the city's entire school system, according to Reed's campaign website. 

Reed, who cites that working-class background as pivotal to his upbringing, attended West Point later in life and spent time in the Army before earning a master's degree in public policy and a law degree from Harvard.

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT FLEXES DOMINANCE AS INSURGENTS FALL AND GOP BENCH THINS IN DEEP BLUE STRONGHOLD

The primary exposed a divide between a more moderate establishment candidate like Reed and the two progressive challengers he faced who ran on issues like abolishing Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE), taxing wealth and ending aid to Israel.

Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, has supported continued military assistance to Israel despite criticizing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and calling for renewed efforts toward a two-state solution.

He was first elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996 after serving three terms in the House, and, in addition to being the ranking Democrat on the Armed Services Committee, Reed serves on the Appropriations, Banking and Intelligence committees.

His campaign reported roughly $3.4 million in total receipts during the 2025-2026 election cycle through Aug. 20 and had nearly $3.1 million in cash on hand, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) records.

By comparison, Burbridge reported raising just over $25,000 through Aug. 20, while the FEC listed no fundraising totals for Muñoz's campaign ahead of the primary.

item.title: NBC reminds pregame viewers about Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini scandal coach and Patriots want to forget
item.description: NBC's pregame show spotlighted the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini scandal before the New England Patriots' season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Vrabel and the New England Patriots want everyone to forget that the coach and the franchise by extension were tied to an embarrassing scandal when the Dianna Russini story surfaced in April.

But here we are on the night the NFL season kicks off and, nope, nobody has forgotten.

NBC, bless their hearts, didn't forget.

THE ATHLETIC PROBES DIANNA RUSSINI AND MIKE VRABEL RELATIONSHIP WHILE CONSIDERING GETTING IN BED WITH THE NFL

On their pregame show prior to the Patriots season-opening game against the Seattle Seahawks, the relationship between Vrabel and Russini was highlighted.

And discussed.

MIKE VRABEL STEPPING AWAY FROM PATRIOTS INDEFINITELY TO SEEK COUNSELING AMID DIANNA RUSSINI CONTROVERSY

"Remember in the offseason, Vrabel missed the final day of the draft in April to seek counseling after photos were published of him and longtime NFL reporter Dianna Russini," host Maria Taylor told the audience before moving on to the acquisition of A.J. Brown and asking if the team is better on paper now.

This is not what the Patriots want. It's definitely not what Vrabel wants because he has mostly declined to answer questions on the topic since training camp opened with one exception when he was asked about that family counseling.

MIKE VRABEL, ONE MONTH AFTER STARTING 'COUNSELING,' TELLS REPORTERS HE LOVES HIS WIFE

Vrabel deflected from the topic that time.

DIANNA RUSSINI'S RELATIONSHIP WITH MIKE VRABEL IN CLEAR VIOLATION OF STANDARDS, THE ATHLETIC'S REVIEW SAYS

He also declined to address the issue last week when The Athletic published its standards review which found the reporter's relationship with Vrabel was "in clear violation" of the media company's standards.

"This team has fully moved past all the offseason stuff," analyst Devin McCourty, a former Patriots safety, said on air. "The Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini stuff, they're not talking about it.

"You won't hear a player mention anything. They're focused solely on this season."

The Patriots may indeed be fully focused on the start of the regular season.

But they do not write the script for the media which may continue to mention the offseason scandal early this season as a way of recapping all that happened to the team and its coach.

And, obviously, if the season in any way goes against expectations and the Patriots struggle, it won't be a reach for reporters to ask if the scandal that dominated national headlines from April to June distracted from any preparation.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

One more thing:

Russini, who resigned from The Athletic following the publishing of her photos with Vrabel, has reportedly vowed to address the issue once she returns to public life. Depending on what narrative that address follows, the Patriots may once again find themselves trying to manage a public relations issue.

(Just a guess here: Russini will find no fault with anything she did during her many-years-old relationship with Vrabel dating back to when he coached the Tennessee Titans).

item.title: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson gets the nod to host the 'Saturday Night Live' season premiere
item.description: Jalen Brunson will host the "Saturday Night Live" season premiere, joining Peyton Manning, LeBron James and Michael Jordan among athlete hosts.
item.content:encoded:
The first batch of hosts for the new season of "Saturday Night Live" has been announced, and New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is about to join an elite group of athletes who have been given the nod.

A group with varying degrees of success.

Brunson will host the season premiere of the long-running sketch comedy series, which — believe it or not, kids — has at times in its 50-plus-year run been very funny. That will air on September 26 with musical guest Katseye.

KNICKS STAR JALEN BRUNSON IS A MAN OF THE PEOPLE, REVEALS THE ONE THING HE CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT

Considering he's done some stuff with WWE, I think Brunson might be one of the athletes who actually does well on SNL.

As I said, over the years, we've seen some athletes who proved to be good actors and a lot who were as stiff as a board and portrayed themselves in just about every sketch.

They put out an SNL sports special back in the late aughts (I downloaded it onto my iPod Touch and would watch it in study hall; that's how late aughts it was), and you'd be surprised how many solid sketches there were with athletes, even if the athlete is not a great actor in the sketch.

I think the best athlete host of all time is, without question, Peyton Manning. In fact, I've even argued that his timing is so good, he probably could've been a supporting player.

His high-water mark was without a doubt the United Way commercial, one of the best commercial parodies of the last 25 years.

Another athlete I thought was pretty solid — and this could prove controversial — was LeBron James.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The best sketch he was in was a bizarre Will Forte fever dream called "The Lyle Kane Show" that I can't find anywhere. So, I pulled the next best LeBron sketch, "Read to Achieve."

I've quoted the line, "Don't give me this; I'm a lefty from Kansas," more times than I'd care to admit. It's so good.

A standard SNL play when the athlete's acting is a little on the wooden side is to put them in a sketch where the other actor does all the work.

Like this gem with Michael Jordan and Al Franken as Stuart Smalley.

And one final move for athletes (not typically the host, though) is to stick them behind the "Weekend Update" desk. One of my favorites was this bit with NHL great Brett Hull.

Hopefully the SNL writers and cast — no, I can't name any of them either — have been using the summer to come up with some great material for Brunson when they reconvene at 30 Rock for the season opener at the end of the month.
